English: perfect is the enemy of good
meaning: Insistence on perfection often precludes the opportunity for something worthwhile.
Vietnamese: Quá cầu toàn thì lỡ mất điều tốt
back-translation: Being too perfectionist makes you miss what is good

English: the chickens come home to roost
meaning: A person's past wrongdoings will return to negatively affect them.
example: Opponents see the latest indictments as a case of the chickens coming home to roost.
example Vietnamese: Phe đối lập xem các cáo trạng mới nhất là một trường hợp gieo gió gặt bão.
back-translation: Sow the wind and you will reap the whirlwind

English: there is a time and place for everything
meaning: Certain things are appropriate at a certain time and place.
Vietnamese: Việc gì cũng phải đúng lúc đúng chỗ
back-translation: Everything must be at the right time and place

meaning: Being mentioned in the media, even in the context of a scandal or controversy, is beneficial to the subject because it brings publicity.
Vietnamese: Được báo chí nhắc đến, dù tai tiếng, vẫn là có lợi
back-translation: Being mentioned in the press, even scandalously, is still beneficial

English: a promise made is a promise kept
meaning: A promise that one makes should be or can be considered a promise that one will certainly honor.
Vietnamese: Đã hứa là phải giữ lời

meaning: Whoever finds something is allowed to keep it.
Vietnamese: Ai nhặt được thì của người đó
back-translation: Whoever picks it up owns it; finders keepers

meaning: One companion is preferable to two.
Vietnamese: Hai người thì vui, thêm người thứ ba thành thừa
back-translation: Two is fun, a third is superfluous

meaning: One cannot accurately judge a person solely by their appearance.
Vietnamese: Chiếc áo không làm nên thầy tu
back-translation: The robe doesn't make the monk

meaning: Old trends, fashions or ideas often return to popularity after a period of decline.
Vietnamese: Cái cũ rồi lại thành mốt mới
back-translation: Old things become the new fashion again

meaning: A period of discomfort or hardship can provide the basis for a period of happiness and joy.
Vietnamese: Hết cơn bĩ cực đến hồi thái lai
back-translation: After hard times come good times

English: comparison is the thief of joy
meaning: Comparing one's own situation with that of others will lead to unhappiness or bitterness.
Vietnamese: So bì với người khác chỉ làm mất niềm vui
back-translation: Comparing yourself with others only takes away joy

English: a little knowledge is a dangerous thing
meaning: A limited understanding of a subject can lead individuals to overestimate their expertise, often resulting in errors or misguided decisions due to false confidence.
Vietnamese: Biết nửa vời là điều nguy hiểm

meaning: People are drawn to others who have different or complementary traits, personalities, or characteristics.
If you commit a crime you will most likely be punished for it.
Vietnamese: Phạm tội rồi cũng phải trả giá
back-translation: If you commit a crime, you'll have to pay for it

meaning: More can be accomplished by a team with a common goal than by individuals.

English: there's a sucker born every minute
meaning: There will always be a great number of fools in the world who can be easily swindled.
Vietnamese: Trên đời chẳng bao giờ thiếu kẻ cả tin dễ bị lừa
back-translation: The world never lacks gullible people who are easy to fool

meaning: Events that have already taken place cannot be changed and actions that have already been committed cannot be undone, so it is best not to dwell on them.
back-translation: What's done is done, let it be

meaning: Tomorrow will bring new opportunities and a fresh start for one's endeavors.
back-translation: Tomorrow the sky will be bright again; tomorrow is another day

meaning: Service staff should give high priority to customer satisfaction.
Near success (or near accuracy) is not adequate.
Vietnamese: Suýt được thì vẫn là chưa được
back-translation: Almost succeeding is still not succeeding

English: it takes all kinds to make a world
meaning: Diversity is essential: the world would be incomplete if everyone were alike; an expression of surprise at a person or people's eccentricity.
Vietnamese: Trên đời có đủ hạng người
back-translation: There are all sorts of people in the world

English: it is easy to be wise after the event
meaning: After one has seen the consequences of a decision, it is easy to tell whether or not the decision was favorable, but it is also too late, since the consequences have already occurred.
Vietnamese: Việc xong rồi mới khôn thì ai chẳng khôn được
back-translation: Anyone can be wise after the thing is done

meaning: A situation where the pressure that a person is under makes them demonstrate their potential.
Vietnamese: Lửa thử vàng, gian nan thử sức
back-translation: Fire tests gold, hardship tests strength

English: love the sinner, hate the sin
meaning: One should not treat people badly because of their faults, but one should not go so far as to accept or approve the faults themselves.
Vietnamese: Ghét tội lỗi nhưng hãy thương người phạm lỗi
back-translation: Hate the sin but love the sinner

English: Rome wasn't built in a day
meaning: It takes a long time to create something complicated or impressive.
Vietnamese: Việc lớn không thể một sớm một chiều mà xong
back-translation: Great work can't be done overnight

English: there is an exception to every rule
meaning: Usually said in a situation when the rule is incorrect and unusable.
Vietnamese: Quy tắc nào cũng có ngoại lệ

English: heaven helps those who help themselves
meaning: A maxim encouraging people to attempt to solve their own problems.
Vietnamese: Hãy tự cứu mình trước khi trời cứu
back-translation: Save yourself before Heaven saves you

meaning: Wealth cannot be obtained without some effort; hence currency is not always available for a prospective purchase.
If one practices an activity enough, one will steadily make progress and eventually be able to master it in time.
Vietnamese: Càng luyện tập càng tiến bộ
back-translation: The more you practice, the more you improve

meaning: Used for consolation, possibly self-consolation, after someone has experienced something unfavorable or unpleasant, and hence an encouragement to make the best of the situation.
Vietnamese: Chuyện gì xảy ra cũng có lý do của nó

English: it's not what you know but who you know
meaning: For success, and especially to obtain employment, one's knowledge and skills are less useful and less important than one's network of personal contacts.
Vietnamese: Quan trọng không phải biết gì mà là quen ai
back-translation: It's not what you know but who you know

English: once a thief, always a thief
meaning: A person found to have stolen another's property will always be marked as a thief.
Vietnamese: Đã một lần ăn cắp thì mãi mang tiếng kẻ trộm
back-translation: Steal once and you're labeled a thief forever

English: a fool and his money are soon parted
meaning: It is difficult or unlikely that careless and irresponsible individuals will maintain their hold on acquired wealth.
Vietnamese: Kẻ dại thì tiền chẳng giữ được lâu
back-translation: A fool can't keep money long

English: there's no business like show business
meaning: The domain of the entertainment industry is more dazzling and exciting than any other business.
Vietnamese: Không nghề nào hào nhoáng như nghề giải trí
back-translation: No profession is as glamorous as the entertainment business

meaning: Enjoy yourself; forget your cares; do not worry.
Vietnamese: Cứ ăn uống vui chơi, gạt hết lo âu
back-translation: Just eat, drink and have fun, put worries aside

English: when one door closes, another opens
meaning: When one opportunity is lost, another opportunity soon becomes available.
back-translation: Heaven never shuts off every way out for people

English: it takes one to know one
meaning: A retort to a negative accusation, implying that the accuser shares the fault.
Vietnamese: Chắc bạn cũng thế nên mới nhận ra
example: Bob: You're an idiot! Tony: Takes one to know one!
example Vietnamese: Bob: Cậu là đồ ngốc! Tony: Có ngốc mới nhận ra đồ ngốc!
back-translation: You must be the same, that's why you noticed

meaning: Even small contributions towards a goal help bring the goal nearer.
Vietnamese: Góp gió thành bão, chút nào cũng quý
back-translation: Many small bits add up; every little bit is precious

meaning: The most important consideration in buying real estate is its location.
Vietnamese: Mua nhà đất, quan trọng nhất là vị trí
back-translation: When buying property, location matters most

meaning: Indicates ambivalence or resignation about the present circumstances; dismisses the previous observations as irrelevant.
Vietnamese: Thôi thì sự đã thế rồi
back-translation: Oh well, it's already happened like that

English: a sorrow shared is a sorrow halved
meaning: Grief can be alleviated by discussing it with someone.
Vietnamese: Nỗi buồn được sẻ chia sẽ vơi đi một nửa

English: you don't get something for nothing
meaning: One cannot expect to receive some benefit if one does not pay for it in some way or does not face a counterbalancing hazard or harm.
Vietnamese: Chẳng có gì tự nhiên mà có
back-translation: Nothing comes from nothing; nothing happens by itself

meaning: Exploit any possible opportunity that arises from difficult situations.
Vietnamese: Đừng bỏ lỡ cơ hội mà khủng hoảng mang lại
back-translation: Don't miss the opportunity a crisis brings

English: one man's terrorist is another man's freedom fighter
meaning: one's view on war and political violence depends on perspective
Vietnamese: Kẻ bị bên này gọi là khủng bố lại là anh hùng của bên kia
back-translation: One side's terrorist is the other side's hero

English: procrastination is the thief of time
meaning: If one puts off doing what one ought to do, one will end up not having enough time to do it properly.
Vietnamese: Trì hoãn là kẻ cắp thời gian
back-translation: Procrastination is the thief of time

meaning: An allusive shortening of lightning never strikes twice in the same place, usually used figuratively.
Vietnamese: Chuyện hiếm gặp khó mà xảy ra lần nữa
back-translation: A rare thing is unlikely to happen again

English: good things come in small packages
meaning: Small gestures of help and kindness matter more than costly and exorbitant bestowals.
back-translation: A small gift with much heart

English: you can't take it with you
meaning: It is not possible to take one's material wealth or possessions to whatever world may await one after death.
Vietnamese: Chết đi chẳng mang theo được của cải
back-translation: You can't take wealth with you when you die

meaning: Advance awareness of a situation, especially a risky one, prepares one to deal with it.
Vietnamese: Biết trước thì phòng được trước
back-translation: Knowing in advance lets you guard in advance; forewarned is forearmed

meaning: A person, place, thing, or situation can be very different from how it seems or appears to be at first glance.
Vietnamese: Vẻ ngoài dễ đánh lừa người ta
example: This algebra problem may look very easy at first glance, but looks can be deceiving.
example Vietnamese: Bài đại số này thoạt nhìn có vẻ rất dễ, nhưng vẻ ngoài dễ đánh lừa người ta.

English: he who laughs last laughs best
meaning: Success is enjoyed more after having previously endured ridicule.
Vietnamese: Cười người hôm trước, hôm sau người cười
back-translation: Laugh at others today, others will laugh at you tomorrow
check note: Warns mockers of payback; loses sweeter final success after enduring ridicule.

English: live by the sword, die by the sword
meaning: One who uses violence can expect a violent response; it is better to try to use peaceful means wherever possible.
Vietnamese: Chơi dao có ngày đứt tay
back-translation: Play with knives and one day you'll cut your hand
check note: Means risky behaviour backfires; violence provoking violent response is weakened.

meaning: People who are wicked must work harder than normal people.
Vietnamese: Số vất vả nên chẳng được nghỉ ngơi
back-translation: Fated to toil, so one gets no rest
check note: Drops wickedness; reads as a hard fate, not the wicked working harder.

English: a rising tide lifts all boats
meaning: A truly good outcome benefits all.
back-translation: When the water rises, the boat rises
check note: Suggests things rising with circumstances; benefit to everyone is not conveyed.

meaning: Different people like different things; there's no accounting for taste.
back-translation: Nine people, ten opinions; everyone thinks differently
check note: About differing opinions or disagreement rather than differing likes and tastes.

English: the captain goes down with the ship
meaning: A leader is ultimately responsible for the penalities of a catastrophe, even if they result from external causes or the misactions of others under the leader's purview.
Vietnamese: Người đứng đầu phải sống chết cùng con thuyền của mình
back-translation: The leader must live and die with their ship
check note: Stresses sharing the ship's fate; bearing ultimate responsibility for failure is only implied.

meaning: One is sure to succeed at a task or event on the third try.
Vietnamese: Quá tam ba bận, lần thứ ba ắt thành
back-translation: Third time is sure to succeed
check note: 'Quá tam ba bận' usually means a three-time limit; muddles the lucky-third sense.

meaning: The tactics or strategies of an adversary can also be used against them.
Vietnamese: Anh làm được thì tôi cũng làm được
back-translation: If you can do it, so can I
check note: Reads as matching ability; the retaliation-in-kind warning is weak.

meaning: To select (a person) for a task, etc.
Vietnamese: chỉ định ai làm việc gì
example: The teacher picked on me to answer the question.
example Vietnamese: Cô giáo chỉ định tôi trả lời câu hỏi.
back-translation: to appoint someone to do something

meaning: To spend free time out of the house.
example: You work too hard. You should get out more.
example Vietnamese: Bạn làm việc nhiều quá. Nên ra ngoài chơi nhiều hơn.
back-translation: get out of the house to unwind

meaning: To duck or take cover, usually to avoid harm. Commonly used as a caution or warning in the imperative.
example: With bullets flying, all I could do was get down and pray.
example Vietnamese: Đạn bay vèo vèo, tôi chỉ biết nằm rạp xuống và cầu nguyện.

meaning: To follow or succeed; to be the successor of.
example: Who came after Richard the Lionheart?
example Vietnamese: Ai là người kế vị Richard Tim Sư Tử?

meaning: To delay the progress of, especially in school.
example: He's a year older than his classmates, because he was held back in second grade.
example Vietnamese: Cậu ấy lớn hơn bạn cùng lớp một tuổi vì bị lưu ban năm lớp hai.
back-translation: to make (a pupil) repeat a year

meaning: To be or become of a like type with others; (especially) to be or become socially accepted.
example: The recluse did not fit in at the party.
example Vietnamese: Con người sống khép kín ấy không hòa nhập được ở bữa tiệc.

meaning: To block something completely and physically.
example: The fat that I drained off the meat clogged up the drain.
example Vietnamese: Mỡ tôi chắt từ thịt ra đã làm tắc ống thoát nước.

meaning: To bypass or circumvent (a problem or obstacle).
Vietnamese: tìm cách lách qua trở ngại
example: If we can't fix this problem, we'll just have to work around it.
example Vietnamese: Nếu không sửa được lỗi này, ta đành phải tìm cách lách qua nó.
back-translation: to find a way around an obstacle

meaning: To follow loyally.
example: Stick with me, and I'll protect you.
example Vietnamese: Cứ đi sát theo tôi, tôi sẽ bảo vệ bạn.

meaning: To affirm the truth or reliability of.
example: Let him in. I'll vouch for his good behaviour.
example Vietnamese: Cho anh ta vào đi. Tôi cam đoan anh ta sẽ cư xử đàng hoàng.

meaning: To become detached or to drop from.
example: A button fell off my coat.
example Vietnamese: Áo khoác của tôi bị rơi mất một chiếc cúc.

meaning: To assume a sitting position from a position lying down.
example: Despite being cancer-ridden, Lorin sat up to greet the visitors.

meaning: To ponder or reflect on a subject.
example: When he has time to think over what he did, he will regret it.
example Vietnamese: Khi có thời gian ngẫm lại việc mình đã làm, anh ta sẽ hối hận.

meaning: To pull something out with a sudden jerk.
example: He suddenly whipped out his gun and pointed it at his doctor.
example Vietnamese: Hắn bất ngờ rút phắt súng ra chĩa vào bác sĩ của mình.

meaning: To dissolve; to part.
To reach
To spend time with somebody; to regularly meet with somebody.
example: After the film, do you want to go hang out?
example Vietnamese: Xem phim xong, bạn có muốn đi chơi tiếp không?
back-translation: go out and gather with friends

meaning: To get past a difficult or stressful situation by thinking or talking about it.
Vietnamese: trải lòng để vượt qua chuyện khó khăn
back-translation: to open one's heart to get through a difficulty
check note: 'Trải lòng' means confiding only; omits thinking the problem through.

meaning: To inform on, to rat out; to tell a person in authority that someone else has done something wrong.
Especially in the form to hang about with (someone): to spend time or be friends with.
example: My daughter likes to hang about with older kids after school.
example Vietnamese: Con gái tôi thích la cà với bọn lớn tuổi hơn sau giờ học.
check note: Pejorative register (loafing, running with a crowd); English is neutral.

meaning: To fall from an upright or standing position to a horizontal or prone position.
Often followed by against or among: to compare with (something); to measure up.
back-translation: to compare with, match up to

meaning: To persist, persevere.
To receive updates or opinions from (someone).
example: Have you heard from Kelly?
example Vietnamese: Bạn có tin gì của Kelly không?

meaning: To make clean, to make satisfactorily neat.
To reschedule (something) to a later date or time.
Vietnamese: dời lại sang lúc muộn hơn
example: The report still hasn't been completed, so the meeting will have to be moved back again.
example Vietnamese: Báo cáo vẫn chưa xong nên cuộc họp lại phải lùi lịch.
back-translation: to postpone to a later time

meaning: To introduce, add or initiate a person or group of people to an organisation or event; to give (someone) a share or portion of something.
Vietnamese: đưa người mới vào tham gia
back-translation: to bring a new person in to participate

meaning: To associate with another in a joint enterprise.
To succeed; to result in a satisfactory situation.
example: Are you still seeing John? - No, it didn't work out.
example Vietnamese: Bạn vẫn đang hẹn hò với John chứ? - Không, chuyện không thành.

meaning: To agonize over (something); to debate a quandary or endeavor to come to a conclusion about a difficult issue.
Vietnamese: trăn trở, vật lộn với một vấn đề
example: I've been wrestling with your problem all night.
example Vietnamese: Tôi đã trăn trở về vấn đề của bạn suốt đêm.
back-translation: to agonise over, wrestle with a problem

meaning: To hastily put on (clothes).
To retract or withdraw (an earlier statement).
example: No, you are not fat; I take it all back.
example Vietnamese: Không, bạn không béo đâu; tôi xin rút lại hết lời đã nói.

meaning: To cause (something or someone) to become.
example: He turned water into wine.
example Vietnamese: Ông ấy biến nước thành rượu.

meaning: To move to the other side of (something, such as an obstruction) by deviating from a direct course or following a curved path.
example: The tide was too high, and we couldn't get around the rocks.
example Vietnamese: Nước triều quá cao, chúng tôi không đi vòng qua mấy tảng đá được.

meaning: To cause to fall to the floor
To transfer (property or rights) to somebody else by signing a document.
example: He signed his house over to his wife in order to avoid taxes.
example Vietnamese: Ông ấy ký chuyển nhượng căn nhà cho vợ để tránh thuế.

meaning: To accept an idea as valid; to join in on a concept.
Vietnamese: tán thành và ủng hộ một ý tưởng
back-translation: to approve of and support an idea

meaning: To become completely known, felt, or understood.
example: He knows he's been naughty, but it will take a while for it to sink in.
example Vietnamese: Thằng bé biết mình đã hư, nhưng phải một lúc nữa nó mới thấm.
back-translation: to gradually sink into the head

meaning: To develop symptoms or signs of (an illness).
example: With a scratchy throat and a cough, it feels like I'm coming down with a cold.
example Vietnamese: Họng ngứa rát lại thêm ho, hình như tôi sắp bị cảm rồi.
back-translation: to be starting to come down with an illness

meaning: To deeply enjoy or be fulfilled by something esteemed as very important in one's life.
example: I live for knowledge.
example Vietnamese: Tôi sống vì tri thức.
back-translation: to regard as one's reason for living

meaning: To examine or inspect something in order to determine its condition; to check out.
example: I will check up on the car tomorrow.
example Vietnamese: Mai tôi sẽ kiểm tra chiếc xe.

meaning: To remain awake; to not go to bed.
example: My plane leaves at 6:00 in the morning, so I plan to stay up until then and sleep on the plane.
example Vietnamese: Máy bay cất cánh lúc 6 giờ sáng, nên tôi định thức đến lúc đó rồi lên máy bay ngủ.
back-translation: stay awake instead of going to bed

meaning: To walk with no planned destination; to meander.
To serve as a model for an artist or as the subject of a piece of art.
Vietnamese: ngồi làm mẫu cho họa sĩ
back-translation: to sit as a model for a painter

meaning: To recover from (a minor injury) or digest (a large meal) by walking around.
Vietnamese: đi lại một lúc cho đỡ
example: It doesn't feel too bad. Let me walk it off.
example Vietnamese: Cũng không đau lắm. Để tôi đi lại một lúc cho đỡ.
back-translation: to walk around a while to make it better

meaning: To distribute; to give out, either by hand or as if so (figuratively).
To fasten (a piece of clothing, etc.); to tighten
example: I can't do up my shirt. The button is missing.
example Vietnamese: Tôi không cài áo được. Mất một cái cúc rồi.

meaning: To act as a replacement or substitute.
back-translation: to step in and do it in someone's place

meaning: To get away, or escape, taking (something) with one.
example: The thieves got away with a million pounds' worth of jewellery.
example Vietnamese: Bọn trộm cuỗm đi số nữ trang trị giá một triệu bảng.

meaning: To fall to the ground. To collapse.
example: The beams supporting the roof had rotted, causing the entire house to fall down.
example Vietnamese: Các thanh xà đỡ mái đã mục, khiến cả căn nhà đổ sập.

meaning: To rely on, trust, or expect.
example: Don't count on being able to get back into the building after 5pm.
check note: Means await or hope for; loses the rely-on and trust sense.

meaning: To begin clanging or making noise.
example: The alarm will go off at six a.m.
check note: Bare 'kêu' is ambiguous; misses an alarm starting to ring.

meaning: To move into (an object), such that one ends up inside it.
example: She got into the car.
example Vietnamese: Cô ấy lên xe.
check note: 'Chui' implies crawling or squeezing in, narrower than get into.

meaning: To come to a final place, condition, or situation, sometimes unplanned or unexpected; to turn out.
example: They ended up angry at each other.
example Vietnamese: Rốt cuộc họ lại giận nhau.
check note: Example 'lại giận nhau' can read as angry again.

meaning: To enter illegally or by force, especially in order to commit a crime.
example: Somebody broke into his car and stole his tools and CDs.
example Vietnamese: Kẻ nào đó đã phá xe anh ấy, lấy trộm đồ nghề và đĩa CD.
check note: Example 'phá xe' reads as wrecking the car, not breaking in.

meaning: To return, restore (a thing to its original owner or location etc.).
example: Give me back my book!
check note: Bare 'trả' also means pay; 'trả lại' is needed for clarity.

meaning: To suddenly start doing or producing something.
check note: Reads as something popping out; misses suddenly starting to do something.

meaning: To resemble (a parent or ancestor) in appearance or habit.
example: She takes after her grandmother with her wide eyes and quiet disposition.
example Vietnamese: Cô ấy giống bà ở đôi mắt to và tính trầm lặng.
back-translation: resemble an adult in the family
check note: 'Adults in the household' is looser than parent or ancestor.

meaning: To diss; to put down.
example: Hey! Quit messing with my brother.
example Vietnamese: Này! Đừng có kiếm chuyện với em tao nữa.
back-translation: to look for trouble and pester
check note: Meaning is insult or put down; Vietnamese says provoke and pester.

meaning: To reply impertinently or rudely; to answer in a cheeky or rude manner.
example: Jane talked back a little too often.
example Vietnamese: Jane cãi lại hơi bị thường xuyên.
check note: Example's slang 'hơi bị' means 'quite often', losing 'too often'.

meaning: To be determined to do or achieve something.
example: I had my mind pretty well set on working for a small company.
example Vietnamese: Tôi đã gần như quyết chí làm cho một công ty nhỏ.
back-translation: to be determined to achieve something
check note: Example 'gần như quyết chí làm cho' is unnatural and ambiguous.

meaning: To lead or take the lead in; to direct; to take charge of.
example: We want you to head up the effort to organize all the entries.
example Vietnamese: Chúng tôi muốn bạn phụ trách việc sắp xếp toàn bộ các mục gửi về.
back-translation: to head and be in charge of

meaning: To worsen; to fail or go amiss; to have a bad outcome.
example: Everything seems to be going very badly wrong today.
example Vietnamese: Hôm nay mọi thứ dường như đều trục trặc hết sức tệ hại.
check note: Awkward collocations, especially 'trục trặc hết sức tệ hại' in the example.

meaning: Depending upon some condition or requirement; provided that; if, assuming; as long as.
example: I don't mind if he stays there, so long as he cleans up after himself when he's done.
back-translation: exempt / as long as / free of (ambiguous single word 'mien')
check note: Bare 'miễn' is ambiguous (exempt); 'miễn là' is clearer.

meaning: Said to someone who has just sneezed, as a polite remark.
check note: Reads as farewell or toast health wish; not clearly a sneeze response.

meaning: An activity or domain in which someone is interested or skilled in; one's personal preference.
check note: 'Sở thích hợp gu' is redundant and unnatural.

meaning: To take care in doing something; to pay attention or ensure that something is done.
Vietnamese: chú tâm làm cho bằng được
example: My wallet is missing! I know I had it earlier: I made a point of bringing it.
example Vietnamese: Ví của tôi mất rồi! Rõ ràng lúc nãy còn: tôi đã cố ý mang theo mà.
back-translation: focus on making sure to do it
check note: 'Cho bằng được' implies determination at all costs, stronger than taking care.

meaning: To settle a dispute or disagreement.
example: The committee made peace and agreed to go with the new plan.
example Vietnamese: Ủy ban đã dàn hòa và đồng ý theo kế hoạch mới.
check note: Example 'dàn hòa' suggests mediating others' quarrel, not settling own dispute.

meaning: Upon cursory examination.
example: This report is certainly not comprehensive; it is more of a "Marketing Division at a glance".
example Vietnamese: Báo cáo này chắc chắn chưa đầy đủ; nó giống bản nhìn lướt về Phòng Tiếp thị hơn.
check note: Example phrase 'bản nhìn lướt' is unnatural Vietnamese for an overview.

meaning: To remove plates, etc. from a table after a meal.
back-translation: clear the dining table / set up the meal table (ambiguous: clear the table)
check note: 'Dọn bàn ăn' can also mean setting the table; direction ambiguous.

meaning: To assume a clear and complete form when separate elements come together; to be fully realized at last.
example: If it weren't for your heroic deed, his evil plan would have fallen into place.
example Vietnamese: Nếu không nhờ hành động anh hùng của bạn, âm mưu của hắn đã trót lọt đâu vào đấy.
check note: Example's 'trót lọt đâu vào đấy' is an unnatural collocation.

meaning: To disturb the status quo or go against rules or conventions, as in an effort to get attention.
example: I'd just jump in and fix it, but that's not my job, and I don't want to rock the boat.
example Vietnamese: Tôi muốn nhảy vào sửa luôn, nhưng đó không phải việc của tôi, và tôi không muốn gây rắc rối.
back-translation: stir up the peace, disturb the calm
check note: 'Khuấy đảo sự yên ổn' is unnatural; 'khuấy đảo' suggests making a splash.

meaning: Greatly enjoys; likes a lot.
example: We'll need to bake more of those new chicken and mushroom pies. The customers can't get enough.
example Vietnamese: Ta cần nướng thêm bánh nhân gà nấm loại mới. Khách ăn mãi không chán.
back-translation: be absorbed and never tire of it
check note: 'Mê mãi' reads like misspelt 'mê mải'; headword phrase sounds unnatural.

meaning: Up to this point, all is OK.
check note: Omits 'so far / up to now', the core of the expression.

meaning: Any assistance, help or aid.
example: Thanks for lending a helping hand to the project.
example Vietnamese: Cảm ơn bạn đã giúp một tay cho dự án.
check note: 'Sự giúp một tay' is an unnatural nominalization.

meaning: Concede to mounting evidence; wake up and smell the coffee.
back-translation: take the hint and act accordingly
check note: Means catching a hint and complying; misses conceding to mounting evidence.

meaning: To confront or deal with directly; to commence a confrontation.
Vietnamese: đối mặt và chấp nhận giải quyết
example: Until she comes to grips with her mother's death, she has no hope of putting it behind her.
example Vietnamese: Chừng nào chưa đối mặt được với cái chết của mẹ, cô ấy không thể nào vượt qua nó.
check note: Headword 'chấp nhận giải quyết' is awkward, reads as 'agree to settle'.

meaning: Very soon.
Vietnamese: sắp đến nơi rồi, bất cứ lúc nào
example: The train will be arriving any time now.
example Vietnamese: Tàu sắp đến bất cứ lúc nào.
check note: Headword tied to arriving; 'sắp ... bất cứ lúc nào' is unnatural.

meaning: A movement from one location to another.
Vietnamese: sự thay đổi không khí, đổi chỗ ở
back-translation: a change of air, change of living place
check note: 'Đổi chỗ ở' implies moving house, narrower than changing location.

meaning: An expression used to convey mild self-deprecation or to acknowledge a mistake or oversight.
example: Oh, silly me! I forgot to buy the apples!
example Vietnamese: Ôi, mình ngớ ngẩn thật! Quên mua táo rồi!
check note: 'Đãng trí' limits it to forgetfulness, not general silly mistakes.

meaning: The past performance of a person, organization, or product, viewed in its entirety and usually for the purpose of making a judgment.
back-translation: past achievements / track record of successes
check note: 'Thành tích' implies achievements only; track record is neutral overall performance.

meaning: In addition to what has been said; furthermore; moreover.
example: He went to a famous school, and a good one at that.
example Vietnamese: Anh ấy học một trường nổi tiếng, mà lại còn là trường tốt nữa chứ.
check note: Headword 'mà lại còn thế nữa' is awkward; example is fine.

meaning: To make one feel comfortable, to seem appropriate or acceptable to.
Vietnamese: khiến người ta thấy ổn thỏa
example: The way you talk to your wife doesn't sit right with me.
example Vietnamese: Cái cách anh nói chuyện với vợ làm tôi thấy không ổn chút nào.
back-translation: make people feel it's all right
check note: 'Thấy ổn thỏa' is unnatural; ổn thỏa describes arrangements, not feelings.

meaning: Certainly; by all means; as a matter of importance.
Vietnamese: nhất định, không được sai sót
example: You will report to the police every week without fail.
example Vietnamese: Anh phải trình diện cảnh sát hằng tuần, tuyệt đối không được bỏ.
check note: 'Không được sai sót' means making no errors, not without fail.

meaning: To pretend or imagine.
example: Let's make believe that we are explorers.
example Vietnamese: Mình giả làm nhà thám hiểm đi.
check note: Without a comma, headword reads as 'pretend to imagine'.

meaning: Well done, to a male.
back-translation: Very good boy / what a good son
check note: Reads as 'obedient son'; loses general 'well done' to any male.

meaning: To be skilled, adept, or graceful with or at (something).
Vietnamese: rất khéo léo trong chuyện xử lý
example: She has a way with animals, and they seem instinctively to trust her.
example Vietnamese: Cô ấy rất khéo với động vật, và chúng dường như tin cô theo bản năng.
check note: 'Trong chuyện xử lý' is unnatural, dangling, and narrower than 'have a way with'.

meaning: To conceal oneself; to remain hidden.
example: I'll lie low here until you get back.
example Vietnamese: Tôi sẽ nấp ở đây cho đến khi anh quay lại.
check note: 'Chờ thời' adds awaiting an opportunity; meaning is just staying hidden.

meaning: Inexperienced; just beginning; immature (especially in judgment).
check note: Stresses being newly arrived; inexperience and immature judgement are weaker.

meaning: As a profession; professionally.
example: Although he was a gifted musician, he was a plumber by trade and never played music professionally.
example Vietnamese: Dù chơi nhạc rất giỏi, anh ấy làm nghề thợ ống nước và chưa từng chơi nhạc chuyên nghiệp.
check note: 'Theo nghề nghiệp' is unnatural; reads as 'according to occupation'.

meaning: Resembling; similar to; in a way; partially or not entirely.
example: He wrote a polite retraction, as an apology of sorts for his harsh words.
example Vietnamese: Anh viết lời rút lại lịch sự, như một kiểu xin lỗi cho những lời gay gắt của mình.
check note: Example's 'viết lời rút lại' is unnatural for writing a retraction.

meaning: To play truant; to avoid (informally: skip) school, work, or other duties (stay away from these without permission nor an excuse); to skive or to bunk off (UK);
example: Plenty of people played hooky from work to go see the movie on opening day.
example Vietnamese: Rất nhiều người trốn làm để đi xem phim trong ngày công chiếu.
back-translation: to skip work to go have fun
check note: Narrowed to skipping work; omits school truancy and other duties.

meaning: Well done, to a female.
check note: Praises a daughter's obedience; misses 'well done' to a female.

meaning: Especially; more than other people
Vietnamese: không ai khác mà lại là
back-translation: none other than, of all people/things
check note: Reads as 'none other than'; 'especially, more than others' is lost.

meaning: On one's hands and knees.
Vietnamese: bò bằng tay và đầu gối
back-translation: to crawl on hands and knees
check note: Adds crawling; the meaning is just being on hands and knees.

meaning: When a valuable potential has finally unfolded into a vibrant reality.
back-translation: the most brilliant level / peak brightness
check note: Can read as peak brightness; potential unfolding into reality is lost.

meaning: To praise or congratulate.
example: Don't pat yourself on the back so vigorously; you might hurt yourself.
example Vietnamese: Đừng tự khen mình hăng quá, coi chừng đau tay đấy.
back-translation: to pat on the shoulder in praise
check note: Example drops the self-patting image, so the sore hand makes little sense.

meaning: A putting down or expression of disdain about something that one desires but cannot have.
example: I think his comments about that new car are just sour grapes because he can't afford it.
check note: Near-literal; disdain for the unattainable is unclear without the fable.

meaning: Not gradually; all at once; referring especially to quitting a habit by force of will rather than by a gradual reduction.
example: It is difficult, but possible to quit smoking cold turkey.
example Vietnamese: Bỏ thuốc lá dứt khoát một lần thì khó, nhưng làm được.
back-translation: to quit decisively once and for all
check note: Reads as 'once and for all'; abrupt, non-gradual quitting is unclear.

meaning: Exactly, to its full degree
check note: Fits only comparisons; 'exactly, to the full degree' is weakly conveyed.

meaning: (Very) inaccurate.
example: Well, I suppose you could say the weatherman was wide of the mark again then!
example Vietnamese: Chà, có thể nói anh dự báo thời tiết lại đoán trật lất rồi!
check note: Example's 'anh dự báo thời tiết' can read as addressing 'you'.

meaning: The practice of flipping a coin in the air, to choose between two alternatives based on which side lands face up.
back-translation: heads or tails (face down or face up)
check note: Gives only the call; coin-toss practice for choosing is not conveyed.

meaning: Feeling sharp anticipation or anxiety; in a state of suspense.
check note: Conveys fidgeting; anxious or eager suspense is weak.

meaning: To take the wrong approach to a situation; to follow a false lead; to attempt to solve a problem using mistaken assumptions about its true nature.
Vietnamese: nhầm hướng ngay từ cách nghĩ
back-translation: going the wrong way from the very way of thinking
check note: Awkward explanatory phrasing, not a natural Vietnamese expression.

meaning: To go unchecked; to be out of control.
back-translation: free to run wild, do as one pleases
check note: Connotes bold free rein; the 'out of control' sense is weakened.

meaning: To lessen or weaken over time, as from overuse.
example: Your jocose wisecracks have already worn thin.
example Vietnamese: Mấy câu đùa cợt của anh đã nhàm lắm rồi.
check note: Narrows to becoming boring; general lessening or weakening is lost.

meaning: (Knowing, remembering, or understanding something) with extreme clarity, especially a painful or highly emotional experience.
check note: Means 'clearer than ever', not 'only too well'; adds a comparison.

meaning: A hierarchy.
example: With my promotion this month I will continue my steady journey to the top of the food chain.
example Vietnamese: Với lần thăng chức tháng này, tôi sẽ tiếp tục vững bước tiến lên đỉnh của thang bậc.
check note: Example's 'đỉnh của thang bậc' is unnatural Vietnamese.

meaning: Rapidly or immediately.
example: Fortunately, help arrived on the double, and the victim's injuries were soon treated.
example Vietnamese: May mà cứu hộ đến rất nhanh, vết thương của nạn nhân sớm được chữa trị.
check note: 'Nhanh lên' reads as the command 'hurry up', not an adverb.

meaning: The final cessation or discontinuance of a process, institution, lineage, or person, especially one which has existed for a considerable period of time; death.
Vietnamese: bước đường cùng, hồi kết thúc
back-translation: the end of the road, the final chapter
check note: 'Bước đường cùng' means desperate straits, not final cessation or death.

meaning: To seem to be correct, or plausible
Vietnamese: nghe có vẻ đúng, đáng tin
example: His excuse about his daughter being ill again rings true, to me.
example Vietnamese: Theo tôi, lời anh ta viện cớ con gái lại ốm nghe có vẻ thật.
check note: Example's 'viện cớ' implies a false pretext and reads awkwardly.

meaning: Not included in the matter being planned or under consideration; not a factor or participant in the present situation.
Vietnamese: không còn liên quan trong cuộc
back-translation: no longer relevant in the contest
check note: 'Không còn liên quan trong cuộc' is awkward; 'ngoài cuộc' sense unclear.

meaning: To allow to be apprehended in its full scope.
back-translation: to show oneself worthy of one's standing; perform up to par
check note: Reads as performing worthily; sense of conveying something's full scope is unclear.

meaning: Expresses that the speaker must go and deal with something.
Vietnamese: Có việc phải đi làm rồi
example: Excuse me, gentlemen, but I'm afraid duty calls.
example Vietnamese: Xin lỗi các anh, e là tôi có việc phải đi rồi.
back-translation: I've got to go to work now
check note: Headword reads as leaving for work, not attending to a duty.

meaning: Well in advance.
Vietnamese: từ xa đã nhận ra trước
back-translation: to recognize in advance from far off; see it coming
check note: Adds the verb 'recognize'; meaning is just 'well in advance'.

meaning: To return to a previous state.
example: We had a terrible year so we agreed to turn back the clock and go on as if it hadn't happened.
example Vietnamese: Chúng tôi đã trải qua một năm tồi tệ nên quyết định quay lại như thể chuyện đó chưa từng xảy ra.
check note: Example 'quay lại' is ambiguous and drops 'go on'.

meaning: A moderate inclination.
Vietnamese: ý định nửa muốn nửa không
example: His behaviour gives me half a mind to throw him out.
example Vietnamese: Cách cư xử của hắn khiến tôi chỉ muốn tống cổ hắn ra ngoài.
check note: Example says 'just want to throw him out', losing the moderate inclination.

meaning: Used to liken one situation to another, typically saying that the existence of one situation is equivalent to the existence of another, usually more extreme, situation.
example: You're going to tell her what I said about her? You might as well shoot me!
example Vietnamese: Cậu định kể với cô ấy những gì tớ nói về cô ấy à? Thế thì bắn tớ luôn đi cho rồi!
check note: Headword means 'would rather do that', not likening to an extreme situation.
